preregistration.expectation: A dvc.yaml pipeline in a fresh git+DVC 3.67.1 scratch repo, whose stages run replay.py materialize and replay.py select over the tracked fixture, completes under `dvc repro`, records a dvc.lock, and after deleting the outputs `dvc checkout` restores them byte-identically. replay.py select against the DVC-restored snapshot returns per-cutoff records and selection_sql_sha256 equal to the project-local path (materialize+select outside DVC), and the unknown-availability mutations still exit 2 when fed through the DVC-restored source.
criteria: C0.1 `dvc repro` exits 0 and dvc.lock pins md5 of every stage dep and out.
C0.2 A second `dvc repro` with unchanged deps skips every stage (reproduction is cache-aware), and `dvc status` reports up to date.
C0.3 After `rm -rf` of every out, `dvc checkout` restores the tree; the sha256 list equals the pre-delete list.

C0.4 For each cutoff in the replay test suite (…099Z, …100Z, …200Z, …201Z) replay.py select on the DVC-restored snapshot returns the same row_ids as tests/test_nanosecond_replay.py asserts and the same canonical records sha256 and selection_sql_sha256 as the project-local arm.

C0.5 Unknown-availability mutations of the DVC-restored source.json (observation available_at removed, universe available_at removed, available_at null) make replay.py materialize exit 2 with status rejected; a detector control (unmutated restored source) exits 0, so the probe can see a non-rejection.

C0.6 `dvc repro --force` regenerates a snapshot whose three data files are byte-identical to the first run and whose snapshot.json differs only in ingested_at; that is the recorded expectation, not a failure.
Refutation: any C0.x failing marks the gap not_settled with the observed failure.

criteria: G0.3a Fresh git+DVC 3.67.1 scratch repo with the same dvc.yaml and stage driver: `dvc repro` exits 0, dvc.lock and the DVC-written .gitignore files are committed, and a second `dvc repro` skips all six stages (re-observes C0.1/C0.2 in this run).

G0.3b As-written arm, kept as the detector: `rm -rf data out; dvc checkout`, then the full-tree sha256 list of data/ and out/ is diffed against the pre-delete list. Expected: the diff exits 1 and the only differing entries are data/.gitignore and out/.gitignore (dvc checkout does not restore git-tracked files). Any other differing entry fails G0.3.

G0.3c Corrected full-tree restore: `rm -rf data out; git checkout -- data/.gitignore out/.gitignore && dvc checkout`, then the full-tree sha256 list diff against the pre-delete list exits 0, and `dvc status` reports up to date.

G0.3d Outs-only delete: remove only the eight DVC outs declared in dvc.yaml (keeping the git-tracked .gitignore files), `dvc checkout`, then the full-tree diff exits 0 and `dvc status` reports up to date.

G0.3e Detector control: after G0.3d, overwrite one byte of data/ns_materialized/observations.parquet; the full-tree diff must exit 1 naming that file and `dvc status` must report a change. Then `dvc checkout --force` restores it and the full-tree diff exits 0 again.

Outcome rule for gap 0: the original run's C0.3 as written stays recorded as failed. Gap 0 is settled only if G0.3a-G0.3e all pass on this fresh run and the original C0.1, C0.2, C0.4, C0.5 and C0.6 results stand; if any G0.3 arm fails, gap 0 is not_settled with the observed failure.

outcome_reason: Under the original preregistration the original run is not_settled: C0.3 as written (full-tree sha256 list after `rm -rf data out; dvc checkout` equals the pre-delete list) failed with git_restore_diff_exit=1, because `dvc checkout` alone does not restore the git-tracked data/.gitignore and out/.gitignore. C0.1, C0.2, C0.4, C0.5 and C0.6 passed as written on native DVC 3.67.1 CLI runs with live-captured logs. The outcome 'settled' follows the fix-round-3 rule (preregistration-fixround3.json, written at 13:20:19Z after the original C0.3 result was seen, committed in 9f84cc9 before the rerun). On a fresh git+DVC repo: G0.3a repro and cache-aware second repro passed; G0.3b (as written, kept as the detector) reproduced exactly the two .gitignore differences; G0.3c (`git checkout -- data/.gitignore out/.gitignore && dvc checkout`) full-tree diff exit 0 on all 16 files; G0.3d (delete only the eight DVC outs, then `dvc checkout`) exit 0 on all 16 files; G0.3e (one-byte overwrite detected by the diff and `dvc status`, then `dvc checkout --force` restores) passed. The runs cover add, restore and pipeline reproduction: a native `dvc add` of a replay.py snapshot directory was restored byte-identically by `dvc checkout`; a dvc.yaml pipeline wrapping replay.py materialize/select and temporal_snapshot.py snapshot/select ran under `dvc repro` with a dvc.lock, and a second repro skipped all six stages; on the DVC-restored snapshots, per-cutoff records and selection_sql_sha256 equal the project-local path and the regression-test assertions; the unknown-availability mutations of the restored source.json exit 2 while the unmutated control exits 0.
limits: Synthetic repository fixtures only (replay: 5 observations, 2 universe rows; point-in-time fixture). No real or licensed market data, and no scale measurement.
Local DVC cache only; no remote storage was configured or tested.

`dvc repro --force` re-materializes a new snapshot.json: ingested_at changes, so snapshot_sha256 changes, while the three data files stay byte-identical. A caller holding the old digest must restore through DVC (checkout) rather than repro. This is the documented contract, recorded as C0.6.

Restore contract: `dvc checkout` restores DVC outs only. After a whole-directory delete, the git-tracked .gitignore files that DVC wrote at repro time come back only from git (`git checkout -- data/.gitignore out/.gitignore`), so a complete restore is git checkout plus dvc checkout (fix round 3, G0.3b/G0.3c).

The fix-round-3 C0.3 criterion was written after the original C0.3 failure was seen; the original run stays recorded as failing C0.3 as written. C0.4-C0.6 were not re-run in fix round 3; they come from the original run.
The DVC stage driver (stage.py) is project harness code. It calls the project CLIs by subprocess, so exit codes are the CLIs' own.
